title: The hosts the fabric operates, and where each account lives
description: runtime/hosts/registry.json. A host id is its short hostname. Placement maps a Linux login to the host it was provisioned on; it is where the account is, never who it is or what role it holds.

ssh.description: An ssh destination for the operator account ([user@]host), or null: the host this registry is read on, reached directly.

sshd.description: The host's own sshd, which the operator's Fleet Deck reaches each placed account through (ADR-048): null or absent until provisioned. Not `ssh`, which is the coordinator's destination for the operator account and null for the local host. `host_keys` are the host's public keys as `<type> <base64>`, read on the host (ssh-operator.sh prints them) and pinned here; `fabric-ssh-hosts known-hosts` writes known_hosts from them and `check` compares them with the host.

address.description: An IP address, not a name: a name would be resolved, and the pin would follow whatever it resolved to. 127.0.0.1 on a single-host deployment.

operator.description: The login on that host that holds sudo and the fabric checkout; the ssh destination logs in as it.

fabric.description: The operator's fabric checkout on that host; ~ is the operator's home there.

operator_key.description: The public half of the operator's control-plane signing key (SPKI DER, base64), written by `fabric-ctl keygen`. Every control daemon answers an ACTION (runtime/control/sign.mjs) only when it is signed with this key; a host without one can order no action. Optional: read ops need no key. The width is exact — an Ed25519 SPKI is always 44 bytes, 59 base64 characters and one `=` — so a truncated or mispadded key fails lint; a same-width value that is not an SPKI is caught by tests/test_hosts_registry.py, which parses the committed key as the daemons do.

kinds.description: A placed login's kind when it is not an agent (ADR-044): human. A login not named here is an agent.
